reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms that melt-spinning at 10^5–10^6 K/s yields an amorphous structure, supporting the premise that high cooling rates suppress crystallization. However, there is no evidence that cryogenic substrate cooling can achieve such rates in bulk samples, nor any data on an intermediate thermal management layer or its effects. The link between suppressed nucleation and enhanced thermal stability is plausible but not directly evidenced.
